questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The speed of sound in oxygen at S.T.P. will be approximately:
(Given, $\left.\mathrm{R}=8.3 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}, \gamma=1.4\right)$
questions.solution:
At STP
Temperature, $T=273 \mathrm{ K}$
Molecular mass of oxygen, $\mathrm{M}=32 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ kg}$
Speed of sound is given by
$\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}=\sqrt{\frac{1.4 \times 8.3 \times 273}{32 \times 10^{-3}}}=314.8541 \simeq 315 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of speed of sound in hydrogen gas to the speed of sound in oxygen gas at the same temperature is:
questions.solution:
Given $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{H}_2}=2 ; \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=32$
Speed of sound, $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}$
$\Rightarrow \quad v \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$
$\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{H}_2}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{H}_2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{2}}=4: 1$

B sends a sonar signal of $600 \mathrm{ Hz}$ to detect $A$ and receives a reflected sound of frequency $v$. The of $v$ is [Speed of sound in water $=1500 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ ]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Transverse waves of the same frequency are generated in two steel wires $A$ and $B$. The diameter of $A$ is twice that of $B$ and the tension in $A$ is half that in $B$. The ratio of the velocities of the waves in $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution: The velocity of transverse waves is given by $v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}$ where, $T=$ Tension and $m=$ mass per unit length of the wire. If $r$ is the radius of the wire and $\rho$ its density then, $m=\pi r^2 \rho\therefore \quad v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{T}{\pi r^2 \rho}}\therefore \quad v_A=\frac{\sqrt{T_A}}{r_A \sqrt{\pi \rho}}$ and $\quad v_B=\frac{\sqrt{T_B}}{r_B \sqrt{\pi \rho}}$ Now, $\quad \frac{v_A}{v_B}=\sqrt{\frac{T_A}{T_B}} \cdot \frac{r_B}{r_A}\because \quad r_A=2 r_B$ and $T_A=\frac{1}{2} T_B$ Hence, $\quad \frac{v_A}{v_B}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: An organ pipe, open from both end produces 5 beats per second when vibrated with a source of frequency $200 \mathrm{ Hz}$. The second harmonic of the same pipes produces 10 beats per second with a source of frequency $420 \mathrm{ Hz}$. The fundamental frequency of organ pipe is

Let the fundamental frequency of organ pipe be $\mathrm{f}$ Case I : $f=200 \pm 5=205 \mathrm{ Hz}$ or $195 \mathrm{ Hz}$
Case II : frequency of 2 nd harmonic of organ pipe $=2 \mathrm{f}$ (as is clear from the second figure) $2 \mathrm{f}=420 \pm 10$ or $\mathrm{f}=210 \pm 5$ or $\mathrm{f}=205$ or 215 Hence fundamental frequency oforgan pipe $=205 \mathrm{ Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two sources of sound $A$ and $B$ are moving towards and away from a stationary observer with the same speed respectively. If the frequency of the sound produced by both the sources is equal to $400$ Hz, then the speed of sources (approximately) if the observer detects 4 beats per second, is [Given, speed of sound $= 340ms^{- 1}$]
questions.solution:
Given, frequency of sound produced by sources $A$~and $B$,~${f}_{A} = {f}_{B} = 400Hz$

Speed of sound in air, $v = 340ms^{- 1}$

Apparent frequency heard by the observer when source $A$ is moving towards him,

${f}_A^{'} = \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{S}} \times {f}_{A} = \dfrac{340}{340 - {v}_{S}} \times 400$

Apparent frequency heard by the observer when source $B$ is moving away from him,

${f}_B^{'} = \dfrac{v}{v + {v}_{s}} \times {f}_{B} = \dfrac{340}{340 + {v}_{s}} \times 400$

Given, Beats~$= {f}_A^{'} - {f}_B^{'} = 4$

$\dfrac{340}{340 - {v}_{s}} \times 400 - \dfrac{340}{340 + {v}_{s}} \times 400 = 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{34000 \times 2{v}_{S}}{{340}^{2} - {v}_S^{2}} = 1$

$\dfrac{34000 \times 2{v}_{S}}{3402} = 1$~ & $\left[∵ {v}_S^{2} < < {340}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ {v}_{s} = 1 . 7ms^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If sound travels in air with the speed of $340ms^{- 1}$, then the number of tones present in an open organ pipe of length $2m$ for a& maximum frequency of $1200$ Hz, are
questions.solution:
Given, speed of sound, $v = 340ms^{- 1}$
Length of open organ pipe, $l = 2m$

Frequency, $f = 1200Hz$
For open organ pipe,

Fundamental frequency, ${f}_{0} = \dfrac{v}{2l} = \dfrac{340}{2 \times 2} = 85$

$∴$ Number of tones present in the open organ pipe
$= \dfrac{f}{f0} = \dfrac{1200}{85} = 14. 11 ≃ 14$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train moves towards a stationary observer with speed $34ms^{- 1}$. The train blows whistle and its frequency is registered by the observer as ${ν}_{1}$. If the train's speed is reduced to $17ms^{- 1},$ then the frequency registered is ${ν}_{2}$. If the speed of sound is $340ms^{- 1}$, then the ratio $\dfrac{ν1}{ν2}$ is
questions.solution:
According to Doppler's effect, the approximate frequency heard by the stationary observer,

$ν = \dfrac{C}{C - {v}_{s}}{ν}_{0}$

Case (I) ${v}_{s} = 34ms^{- 1}$, where& $C =$Speed of sound in air,

${v}_{s} =$ Speed of source, and& ${ν}_{0} =$ frequency of the source.

$∴ {ν}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{340}{340 - 34}\right){ν}_{0}

$= $\dfrac{340}{306} {ν}_{0} . . . . \left($ i\right)$

Case (ii) ${v}_{s} = 17ms^{- 1}$
$∴ {ν}_{2} = $\dfrac{340}{340 - 17} {ν}_{0} = \dfrac{340}{323} {ν}_{0} . . . .\left(ii\right)

From Eq. (i)$ and (ii), we get

∴ $\dfrac{ν1}{ν2} = \dfrac{340 / 306}{340 / 323} = \dfrac{323}{306} = \dfrac{19}{18}$

questions.q: A whistle of frequency $500$ Hz tied to the end of a string of length $1. 2m$ revolves at $400rev\min^{- 1}$. A listener standing some distance away in the plane of rotation of whistle hears frequencies in the range. (Speed of sound $= 340ms^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
${v}_{s} = r\omega = 1 . 2 \times 2\pif$~ & $\left[∵ \omega = 2\pif\right]$

$= 1 . 2 \times 2 \times 3 . 14 \times \left(\dfrac{400}{60}\right) = 50ms^{- 1}$

${v}_{min} = \dfrac{v}{v + {v}_{s}} \cdot v$

$= 436Hz$

$= \dfrac{340}{340 - 50} \times 500$

$= 586Hz$

questions.q:
A transverse wave propagating on a stretched string of linear density $3 \times {10}^{- 4}{kgm}^{- 1}$ is represented by the equation

$y = 0. 2sin ( 1. 5x + 60t )$

where, $x$ in metres and $t$ is in seconds. The tension in the string (in Newton) is
questions.solution:
Equation of wave,&

$y = 0. 2sin [ 1. 5x + 60t ]$

Comparing with standard equation, we get

$y = Asin [ kx + \omegat ]$

$k = 1. 5 = \dfrac{2\pi}{λ}$

and $\omega = 60 = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

$∴$ Velocity of wave, $v = \dfrac{ω}{k}$

$= \dfrac{60}{1. 5} = 40ms^{- 1}$

Velocity of wave in stretched string, $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}}$

where, $m$ is the linear density, $T$ is tension in the string.

So, $T = v^{2}m = ( 40{)}^{2} \times 3 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$= 0. 48N$

questions.q: A string of length $\ell$ is fixed at both ends. It is vibrating in its $3^{\text{rd }}$ overtone with maximum amplitude'a'. The amplitude at a distance $\ell / 3$ from one end is
questions.solution: For a string vibrating in its $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th }}$ overtone $(\mathrm{n}+1)^{\text{th }}$ harmonic) $\mathrm{y}=2 \mathrm{ A} \sin \left(\frac{(\mathrm{n}+1) \pi \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{L}}\right) \cos \omega \mathrm{t}    \begin{array}{l}\text{ For } \left.x=\frac{\ell}{3}\right]2 A=a \& n=3 \\ y=\left[a \sin \left(\frac{4 \pi}{\ell} \cdot \frac{\ell}{3}\right)\right] \cos \omegat\\ =a \sin \frac{4 \pi}{3} \cos \oomegat=-a\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \cos \omegat \end{array}$ i.e. at $x=\frac{\ell}{3},$ the amplitude is $\frac{\sqrt{3} a}{2}$

questions.q: A source of sound S emitting waves of frequency $100 \mathrm{ Hz}$ and an observor $\mathrm{O}$ are located at some distance from each other. The source is moving with a speed of $19.4 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the source observer line as shown in the figure. The observor is at rest. The apparent frequency observed by the observer is (velocity of sound in air $330 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
Here, original frequency of sound, $\mathrm{f}_{0}=100 \mathrm{ Hz}$ Speed of source $V_{s}=19.4 \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}=9.7$
From Doppler's formula $\mathrmf^{\mathrm{l}}=\mathrm{f}_{0}\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{V}_{0}}{\mathrm{ V}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}}\right)\mathrmf^{\mathrm{l}}=100\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}-0}{\mathrm{ V}-(+9.7)}\right)\mathrmf^{\mathrm{l}}=100 \frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}\left(1-\frac{9.7}{\mathrm{ V}}\right)}\mathrmf^{1}=100\left(1+\frac{9.7}{330}\right)=103 \mathrm{ Hz}$ Apparent frequency $\mathrmf^{1}=103 \mathrm{ Hz}$

questions.q: Two waves of wavelengths $99 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $100 \mathrm{ cm}$ both travelling with velocity $396 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ are made to interfere. The number of beats produced by them per second is
questions.solution: Velocity of wave $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{n} \lambda$ where $n=$ frequency of wave $\Rightarrow n=\frac{v}{\lambda}\mathrm{n}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{2}}{\lambda_{2}}=\frac{396}{100 \times 10^{-2}}=396 \mathrm{ Hz}$ no. of beats $=\mathrm{n}_{1}-\mathrm{n}_{2}=4$

questions.q: The fundamental frequency of an open organ pipe is $300 \mathrm{ Hz}$. The first overtone of this pipe has same frequency as first overtone of a closed organ pipe. If speed of sound is $330 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$, then the length of closed organ pipe is
questions.solution:
For open pipe, $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell},$ where $\mathrm{n}_{0}$ is the
fundamental frequency of open pipe. $\therefore \ell=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{n}}=\frac{330}{2 \times 300}=\frac{11}{20}$
As freq. of 1 st overtone of open pipe $=$ freq. of 1 st overtone of closed pipe
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad 2 \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell}=3 \frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell^{\prime}} \Rightarrow \ell^{\prime} &=\frac{3 \ell}{4}=\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{11}{20} \\ &=41.25 \mathrm{ cm} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wave $y=a \sin (\omega t-k x)$ on a string meets with another wave producing a node at $\mathrm{x}=0.$ Then the equation of the unknown wave is
questions.solution:
Equation of a wave $y_{1}=a \sin (\omega t-k x)$....(i)
Let equations of another wave may be, $y_{2}=a \sin (\omega t+k x)$....(ii)
$y_{3}=-a \sin (\omega t+k x) \quad \ldots.$ (iii)
If Eq. (i) propagate with Eq. (ii), we get $\mathrm{y}=2 \mathrm{a} \cos \mathrm{kx} \sin \omega \mathrm{t}$
If Eq. (i), propagate with Eq. (iii), we get $y=-2 a \sin k x \cos \omega t$
At $x=0, y=0,$ wave produce node So, Eq.(iii) is the equation of unknown wave

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two tuning forks $A$ and $B$ sounded together give 6 beats per second. With an air resonance tube closed at one end, the two forks give resonance when the two air columns are $24 \mathrm{ cm}$ and 25 $\mathrm{cm}$ respectively. Calculate the frequencies of forks.
questions.solution:
Let the frequency of the first fork be $\mathrm{f}_{1}$ and that of second be $\mathrm{f}_{2}$
We then have, $\mathrm{f}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \times 24}$ and $\mathrm{f}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \times 25}$
We also see that $\mathrm{f}_{1} > \mathrm{f}_{2}
\therefore \mathrm{f}_{1}-\mathrm{f}_{2}=6 and \frac{\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\frac{24}{25}$
Solving (i) and (ii), we get $\mathrm{f}_{1}=150 \mathrm{ Hz}$ and $\quad \mathrm{f}_{2}=144 \mathrm{ Hz}$
